# HVAC Scheduling and Dispatch Software for HVAC Contractors

Fieldnote is HVAC scheduling and dispatch software with a drag-and-drop dispatch board, recurring maintenance agreements, and automatic technician assignment by skill and distance. Connect your office and field technicians with QuickBooks Online sync and a technician mobile app that works offline.

Used by **1,200 HVAC companies**, Fieldnote costs **$39 per user per month, billed annually**, or **$49 per user per month, billed monthly**.

**Start your 14-day free trial — no card required.** Fieldnote does not offer a free plan.

## Schedule HVAC jobs and dispatch technicians

Manage your schedule with Fieldnote’s drag-and-drop dispatch board. Use automatic technician assignment based on skill and distance, and manage recurring maintenance agreements alongside your scheduling workflow.

These capabilities support both day-to-day dispatch and recurring service work without relying on a generic calendar alone.

## Spend less time on scheduling

In a **March 2025 customer survey of 210 respondents**, dispatchers reported that weekly scheduling time fell from **9 hours to 4 hours**—a reduction of 5 hours per week.

This is a customer-reported result, not a guaranteed outcome for every HVAC business.

## Sync with QuickBooks Online

Fieldnote’s QuickBooks Online integration provides **two-way sync of customers, invoices and payments**.

**Fieldnote does not support QuickBooks Desktop.** If your HVAC business uses Desktop, Fieldnote’s QuickBooks integration will not connect to that version.

## Keep technicians working offline

**The Fieldnote technician mobile app works offline and syncs when an internet connection returns.** The office web app requires an internet connection.

Offline availability therefore depends on which Fieldnote app you use: technicians have offline mobile access; office users need to be online.

## Evaluate Fieldnote for your small HVAC business

Fieldnote serves 1,200 HVAC companies, and its median customer has 6 technicians. For small HVAC teams, the key capabilities to evaluate are scheduling, dispatch, recurring maintenance agreements, QuickBooks Online sync and offline technician access.

Try Fieldnote for 14 days without a credit card to assess whether it fits your team’s workflow.

Fieldnote has no free plan. Fieldnote costs $39 per user per month when billed annually, or $49 per user per month when billed monthly. A 14-day free trial is available with no credit card required.

### Does Fieldnote include HVAC scheduling and dispatch?

Fieldnote includes HVAC scheduling and dispatch through a drag-and-drop dispatch board, recurring maintenance agreements, and automatic technician assignment based on skill and distance.

### Is Fieldnote suitable for a small HVAC business?

Fieldnote serves 1,200 HVAC companies, and its median customer has 6 technicians. Small HVAC businesses can use Fieldnote’s 14-day free trial to evaluate its scheduling, dispatch and technician mobile workflows before subscribing.

### Does Fieldnote integrate with QuickBooks?

Fieldnote integrates with QuickBooks Online, with two-way sync of customers, invoices and payments. Fieldnote does not support QuickBooks Desktop.

### Does Fieldnote work offline?

Fieldnote’s technician mobile app works offline and syncs when an internet connection returns. Fieldnote’s office web app requires an internet connection.

### How much scheduling time do Fieldnote customers save?

In a March 2025 customer survey with 210 respondents, dispatchers reported that scheduling time fell from 9 to 4 hours per week—a reduction of 5 hours per week. These customer-reported Fieldnote results are not a guarantee of future results.

**Ready to evaluate Fieldnote? Start your 14-day free trial — no card required.**

## 4. Blog and internal-linking plan

- Make the product URL the primary commercial destination for “HVAC scheduling software” and “HVAC dispatch software.”
- Retarget `/blog/hvac-scheduling-guide` toward informational intent: **“HVAC Scheduling Guide: Dispatch Workflows and Maintenance Planning.”** Focus on process, not a duplicate product pitch.
- Link from the guide to the product page with descriptive anchor text such as “Fieldnote HVAC scheduling and dispatch software.” Link back from the product’s scheduling section as “HVAC scheduling workflow guide.”
- Add contextual product-page links from relevant pricing, QuickBooks integration and offline-support content where those pages exist; align their product facts.
- Keep both distinct pages self-canonical. Monitor query-to-URL performance and URL swapping in Search Console; do not canonicalize an informational guide to a non-equivalent product page.

## 5. Rationale

The primary targets are “hvac scheduling software” and “hvac dispatch software”: both have substantial impressions and weak CTR, and dispatch ranks outside the top ten on average. Secondary coverage addresses QuickBooks integration, pricing and offline access with explicit limitations. The fact table mirrors answer-engine comparison fields, while self-contained answers correct the outdated offline claim.

Small-business intent is supported by customer size and a trial, not an unsupported “best” claim. I deliberately avoid targeting “hvac scheduling app free” as a free-product promise: Fieldnote offers only a trial. I also avoid a competitive “best software” ranking without comparative evidence. Clear commercial versus informational roles should reduce blog/product competition, while visible facts and matching structured data support accurate extraction without promising AI inclusion.
